comment: Registry of external services reachable through the generic api_call tool. Adding a service here (base_url, credential source, auth, allowed paths/methods, spend rule) is the config-not-code path: no Python adapter needed. The security gates around these entries (SSRF, Jev classification, rate limit, one-strike, page/spend accrual) live in serve.py and are never delegated to this file. path_rules prefixes are matched against the URL path under base_url.

spend.note: Free keyless weather forecasts and current conditions for any lat/lon, no account or quota needed for light use. Reach for it whenever a task needs real current weather or a multi-day forecast for a place (pair with open-meteo-geocoding to turn a place name into coordinates first).

pricing.note: Free keyless forecasts; no account charge. Fair-use rate limits only.

spend.note: Free keyless geocoding: turn a place name or address into latitude/longitude (and vice versa). Reach for it to resolve a city/region name into coordinates before calling the weather API or any other lat/lon-based service.

pricing.note: Free keyless geocoding; no account charge.

spend.note: Read-only access to public GitHub data: repositories, file contents, issues, releases, commit history, and user/org profiles. Reach for it when a task needs real source code, a repo's README/changelog, open issues, or release notes straight from GitHub instead of a scraped page.

pricing.note: Public GitHub REST API is free. Unauthenticated requests are rate-limited (60/hour per IP).

spend.note: Real web search that returns clean, ranked result snippets (the search behind research tasks). Reach for it when you need to find current pages on a topic and do NOT already know a specific URL -- it is a search, not a page fetch. Counts against a monthly budget, so prefer browse_page when you already have the exact URL.

pricing.note: One page request per search. Tavily list price is about $0.008 per basic credit; the tank's monthly page-request cap is the enforced limit.

spend.note: Run pre-built scrapers/crawlers (actors) against websites that block plain fetches, and pull the structured results from datasets. Reach for it when a page is JS-heavy, login-walled, or paginated in a way browse_page cannot handle, or when you need to scrape many pages at scale. Each actor run costs money against a monthly budget, so use it only when cheaper approaches fail.

pricing.note: Actor runs are priced per actor and usage, so there is no single per-call price. Pass maxTotalChargeUsd in the run input; the monthly Apify budget is the hard cap.

spend.note: Generate images from a text prompt (async job: submit, then poll for the finished image). Reach for it when a task needs a real generated image rather than an existing photo. Returns a job you poll; not instant.

pricing.note: Published list prices. The API returns real usage.usd per call, which is logged; estimates use these buckets and may differ slightly.

spend.note: Submit video/image generation jobs (via partner models) and poll for completion. Reach for it when a task needs generated video or motion content. Async: submit a request, then poll the requests endpoint until it finishes.

pricing.note: Credit-based generation; the workflow logs the real balance delta. Check the quote/credit before submitting a large job.

spend.note: Live and historical civil aircraft ADS-B data: current air positions, flight tracks, and departures/arrivals by airport or bounding box. Reach for it when a task needs real live air traffic or a specific flight's path. Standard account, ~4,000 credits/day; heavier endpoints cost more credits.

pricing.note: Free API with a daily call limit; no USD charge.

spend.note: Free keyless live ADS-B aircraft positions (neighborhood of a point, by hex/flight, or by airport). Reach for it for quick live air-traffic lookups without an account. Fair-use rate limits, no uptime guarantee -- prefer it over OpenSky for light/keyless checks.

pricing.note: Free keyless ADS-B; fair-use rate limits only.

spend.note: Free keyless NORAD orbital element sets (TLE data) for satellites and rocket bodies. Reach for it when a task needs to know what satellites are in orbit, a satellite's identity/orbit, or data to propagate a position with an SGP4 library.

pricing.note: Free keyless orbital data; no account charge.

spend.note: Public-transit data: transit agencies, routes, stops, and schedules across many cities. Reach for it when a task needs real transit routes/operators/feeds (e.g. Charlotte CATS). Free tier ~10k REST queries/month; routing API is a separate quota. Attribution to transit.land required. Stop geography can be sparse for some agencies.

pricing.note: Free tier with a daily call limit; no USD charge.

spend.note: Free keyless reader: fetch any public URL and get back clean markdown instead of raw HTML. Reach for it to read a webpage's real content when browse_page returns navigation junk or a JS-heavy shell -- especially useful as a cheap fallback before spending an Apify run.

pricing.note: Free keyless reader; fair-use rate limits only.

spend.note: Live AIS ship-tracking data, but it is WebSocket-only (wss://stream.aisstream.io/v0/stream) with no REST endpoint, so the generic HTTP api_call tool CANNOT stream it. The think tank has a dedicated read_ais_feed collector for the live feed instead. This registry entry only documents the key; use read_ais_feed for real vessel positions.

pricing.note: Free live AIS WebSocket feed; no REST per-call charge. This service is not reachable through api_call.

spend.note: Account status for the think tank's Mullvad VPN account (expiry, device slots, payment). It cannot route a fetch through a foreign exit. To fetch a page as if from another country, use browse_page's exit parameter -- a named sandbox VPN container with its own WireGuard tunnel (see GET /api/vpn-exits) -- or its country parameter for the host's own Mullvad tunnel.

pricing.note: Account/device management only; no per-call USD charge. The VPN tunnel is a shared host resource, not a metered API call.

spend.note: Discover and pull open AI models/datasets from the Hugging Face Hub. /api/ paths give free model metadata, files, and gated-model info; /v1/ is the paid Inference Providers chat router (separate spend). Reach for it to find a model, read its card/config, or download weights (e.g. to run on Colab). Gated models need the license accepted on the account before their files are downloadable.

pricing.note: /api/ metadata and file listing are free. Inference Providers are billed per model and token; check the model card before a paid /v1/ call.

spend.note: Keyless vulnerability database queries; POST a package list to /v1/querybatch and get back known advisories. The dependency audit job uses it; agents can also check a single package via /v1/query.

pricing.note: Free, no key, no quota worth watching (be reasonable).

spend.note: Keyless full-text search over Hacker News stories and comments plus front-page/top lists. Good for "what does HN think about X" and finding discussion threads on a topic.

pricing.note: Free, no key; light rate limits.

spend.note: Keyless Atom search over the full arXiv corpus (all categories, fielded queries like all:electron+AND+all:spin). The RSS feeds cover new cs.LG/cs.CL/cs.SE/cs.AI listings; use this for targeted literature search instead.

pricing.note: Free, no key; be gentle (1 request every ~3s).

spend.note: Keyless archive lookup and capture. /wayback/available/ finds the closest archived snapshot of a URL (evidence for claims after a page changes); /save/ requests a fresh snapshot of a page you are citing -- Rule 10 provenance.

pricing.note: Free, no key; captures are rate-limited, snapshot what you cite, not everything.

spend.note: Keyless paper search, citation and reference graphs, TLDR summaries. Expect frequent 429s (shared public pool) -- retry with backoff or fall back to arXiv search.

pricing.note: Free, no key; rate-limited (429s are normal -- back off and retry).

spend.note: Keyless DOI and bibliographic metadata lookup: verify a paper title/DOI/authors before citing it, resolve a DOI to its landing page. Politeness pool -- set a real User-Agent.

pricing.note: Free, no key; courtesy rate limits (keep the User-Agent honest).

spend.note: TomTom free plan: MONTHLY allowances per product (developer.tomtom.com/pricing); the daily cap below is floor(monthly/31) so 31 running days can never exceed the month. Key is the vault credential tomtom_api_key, injected as ?key= automatically -- agents never handle the key. Search API free tier: 2,500 calls/month -> 80/day.

pricing.note: Free tier 2,500 requests/month. Use poiSearch for businesses/POIs near a lat/lon (params: lat, lon, radius in meters 50-50000, limit).

spend.note: TomTom free plan: MONTHLY allowances per product (developer.tomtom.com/pricing); the daily cap below is floor(monthly/31) so 31 running days can never exceed the month. Key is the vault credential tomtom_api_key, injected as ?key= automatically -- agents never handle the key. Geocoding API free tier: 20,000/month -> 645/day.

pricing.note: Free tier 20,000 requests/month. geocode/{address}.json turns an address or place name into lat/lon.

spend.note: TomTom free plan: MONTHLY allowances per product (developer.tomtom.com/pricing); the daily cap below is floor(monthly/31) so 31 running days can never exceed the month. Key is the vault credential tomtom_api_key, injected as ?key= automatically -- agents never handle the key. Routing API free tier: 20,000/month -> 645/day.

pricing.note: Free tier 20,000 requests/month. calculateRoute/{lat1},{lon1}:{lat2},{lon2}/json?travelMode=car&routeType=fastest returns route summaries (travelTimeInSeconds, trafficDelayInSeconds, lengthInMeters). Summaries only; omit instructionsType (value "none" is rejected).

tomtom-traffic.name: TomTom Traffic Incidents

spend.note: TomTom free plan: MONTHLY allowances per product (developer.tomtom.com/pricing); the daily cap below is floor(monthly/31) so 31 running days can never exceed the month. Key is the vault credential tomtom_api_key, injected as ?key= automatically -- agents never handle the key. Traffic Incidents free tier: 2,500/month -> 80/day.

pricing.note: Free tier 2,500 requests/month. traffic/services/5/incidentDetails?bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat&timeValidityFilter=present returns live incidents (iconCategory, delay, roadNumbers, events). bbox max area 10,000 km^2.

tomtom-traffic.spend_note: ENDPOINT SYNTAX (verified): v5 GET /traffic/services/5/incidentDetails?bbox=-80.95,35.15,-80.70,35.40&language=en-US -- bbox is minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat and v5 takes NO fields param (fields={...} is v4 syntax; mixing it into v5 returns 400). Legacy v4 /traffic/services/4/incidentDetails is also allowed and DOES take fields={...}.

spend.note: Eventbrite v3 with the vault key (header Bearer). NOTE: the public event-search (Discovery) endpoint is RETIRED (404); what works is object fetches by id -- /v3/events/{id}/, /v3/venues/{id}/, /v3/users/me/. Event DISCOVERY needs Ticketmaster Discovery API (free key, to be registered) or an events scraper.

pricing.note: Free with the operator key; read-only GET only.

overpass.name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap)

spend.note: Keyless and free (public OpenStreetMap infrastructure). POI/business density: GET /api/interpreter?data=<QL> or POST with data=<QL>. Rate-limit etiquette applies (~1-2 req/s, no hammering); cap is politeness, not billing. Pairs with tomtom-search: Overpass has category density, TomTom has named businesses.

pricing.note: Free, no account. Keep queries bounded (bounding box + timeout) or the server rejects them.

overpass.spend_note: QUERY SYNTAX (verified): Overpass bbox order is (south,west,north,east) = (minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon) -- DIFFERENT from TomTom (lon first). Working example: data=[out:json][timeout:60];node["amenity"="cafe"](35.15,-80.95,35.40,-80.70);out count; URL-encode the whole QL string as the data param; for POST send it as the raw body. out count; returns element totals without listing every node. INSTANCE BEHAVIOR (verified 2026-10-30): the public primary FLAPS -- 502/406/timeout windows are common and identical queries succeed minutes apart. On 502, 406, or timeout: RETRY the same query up to 3 times with ~5s pauses before declaring the service failed. A 400 Bad Request usually means malformed QL (check bbox order south,west,north,east and quoting).

spend.note: Free public downloads of Redfin housing data (gzipped TSVs, multi-MB, refreshed monthly). Browse https://www.redfin.com/us-data-center for the current file paths, then fetch here. Cap is bandwidth politeness.

pricing.note: Free download; cite Redfin per their data terms.

spend.note: The event-DISCOVERY endpoint Eventbrite retired. Free tier: 5,000 calls/day documented, 5 calls/second -- cap sits at 90% of the documented daily allowance. Key is the vault credential ticketmaster_api_key, injected as ?apikey= automatically. Endpoints: /discovery/v2/events.json (keyword, latlong or city/stateCode/countryCode, radius, unit, startDateTime/endDateTime, size, page, sort), attractions.json, venues.json, classifications.json. Pace requests >= 200ms apart.

pricing.note: Free tier 5,000 calls/day; overage needs a paid contract. Attribution "Powered by Ticketmaster" is required on public surfaces per their terms.

channels.comment: Named read-only channels for platforms the think tank cannot fetch directly (server IPs are blocked). Each channel maps a set of hostnames to an ORDERED backend chain -- the first backend that answers wins, and the chain falls through on failure, mirroring agent-reach's per-platform ordered backends. Backends reference registered services (by id) plus a url_template that rewrites the requested URL into the backend's URL ({url} is the agent's original URL). Jina Reader is the free keyless backend; add a vetted credential-backed backend to a chain by appending it -- first working wins.
